title: The 5 Hottest Record-Breaking Peppers, Ranked (#1 Beats 500 Jalapeños)

scenes.text: The five hottest record-breaking peppers, ranked. Number one floored the man who bred it.
Number five: the ghost pepper. One million Scoville units, two hundred jalapeños. Record holder in 2007.
scenes.label: Ghost pepper · 1M SHU

scenes.text: Number four: the Naga Viper. One point three eight million units, crowned in 2011.
scenes.label: Naga Viper · 1.38M SHU

scenes.text: Number three: the Trinidad Scorpion Butch T. One point four six million, champion for about three years.
scenes.label: Butch T · 1.46M SHU

scenes.text: Number two: the Carolina Reaper, 2013. One point six four million, as hot as police pepper spray.
scenes.label: Carolina Reaper · 1.64M SHU

scenes.text: Number one: Pepper X, 2023. Two point six nine million, over 500 jalapeños. Its breeder felt the heat for three and a half hours, then lay groaning for an hour.
scenes.label: Pepper X · 2.69M SHU

description:
The five hottest peppers to hold the hottest-chilli title, ranked by Scoville heat units.
Ghost pepper (about 1 million SHU, 2007), Naga Viper (1.38 million, 2011), Trinidad Scorpion Butch T (1.46 million), Carolina Reaper (1.64 million, 2013) and Pepper X (2,693,000 SHU, certified by Guinness World Records in October 2023). A jalapeño averages about 5,000 SHU. Pepper X's breeder, Ed Currie, said he felt the heat for three and a half hours before the cramps came.
Which of these would you dare to try?
first_comment: Which would you put at number one? Only five people have ever eaten a whole Pepper X. What should we rank next?
